shared-needs.text: Declared, not linked: the shared author writes these volumes and anchors; check.sh matches each need against shared/ when it lands. Nothing below points at a file that does not exist in this pull request.
shared-needs.need: 100 exists or in progress: seat.bundle, workspace, seat.heartbeat, pr.opened, ticket-set.draft; acts: the next node on the edge

412 precondition refused: seat.bundle.refused, workspace.refused (claim_overlap, aggregate, ticket_in_flight, head_moved), seat.result preflight (bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, lease_expired); acts: N-11, or N-03 for claim_overlap without an attempt
500 failed after 3 or a defect: seat.bundle.failed, workspace.failed, phase.failed, validator.failed, launcher.defect; acts: N-11, or N-06 health then N-28 for a defect

the exact claude -p flag set of N-15 section command (settings, --setting-sources local, --strict-mcp-config, dontAsk, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd, --output-format json, --json-schema, --session-id or --resume); no --fallback-model, no bypassPermissions on the host
max_turns, max_budget_usd, wall_clock_seconds, stall_seconds are role schema fields and launcher arguments, never prose the model counts
every wait has a timeout and a fallback; no agent is a gate; nothing starts by typing; the system drives (dag.md section 7 rule 2 until the shared volume lands)
build mode is a flag with an expiry (N-44) frozen into the dispatch and stamped on the bundle; it never applies to the rebuild's own governance except where a node volume says so
records: the append-only record table with the envelope (id, kind, code, at, node, attempt, idempotency_key, version) and compare-and-swap on version
build_mode: the current flag state with expires_at, written by N-44, read by N-07 at dispatch

section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-13 turns one dispatch record into one seat bundle: the exact files and numbers a one-shot seat is launched with, rendered by code from the role file in the repository and from the ticket's declared files, never typed and never read from the user layer.

It exists because today a seat loads about 44k tokens of user preamble, the architect's private memory, user MCP servers with cluster credentials and a global formatter hook before it reads its ticket (rebuild/investigation/L11-governance-layer.md#52-findings-f1-to-f18 F6, F7, F8, F9), and because build mode exists only as a memory note that nothing enforces (L11 F1). Under D13 the launch command and the repository decide what a seat loads, and build mode is a flag with an expiry that this render reads (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#15-d13-seat-governance-layer-and-the-build-mode-switch).
The bundle is data with a hash. The launcher (N-15) runs exactly the bundle; a seat cannot be launched from anything that is not a committed seat.bundle record.

section.title: Input record: dispatch
section.text: Kind dispatch, code 100, written by N-07. The fields this node reads:
section.field: The dispatch id; it becomes run_id for every record of the run, so every step is idempotent by it.
Ticket id, absent for a spec-author dispatch that works from a design anchor.
worker, spec-author or reviewer. validator is never dispatched to a seat (N-18 is code).
worker, reviewer or spec-author; names which brief template renders.
1 to 3, from N-11.
UTC; the launcher kills the run at this time.
holder, token, generation, expires_at from N-02; copied into the bundle so the launcher's heartbeats carry the fencing token.
Repository slug and the origin URL.
on or off plus expires_at, read by N-07 from the build-mode.state record of N-44 at dispatch time and frozen into the dispatch.

For a reviewer: pr number and head_sha. For a spec-author: design anchor, group, and verdict_ref (the validator.refused record id on a retry). For a worker on attempt n+1: the failure record id (review.changes, merge.conflict, seat.result blocked) to attach.
section.text: Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/dispatch. The canonical envelope (id, kind, code, at, node, attempt, idempotency_key, version) is owned by the shared store volume; this schema repeats it so the volume is whole on its own.

section.title: Output record: seat.bundle
section.text: Kind seat.bundle, code 100, idempotency_key equal to the dispatch id. Fields:
section.field: Equals dispatch.id.
As dispatched.
$COQ_STATE/seats/bundles/<run_id>/ (section state-paths).
bundle_dir/settings.json rendered from roles/<role>.json.
bundle_dir/mcp.json, an empty server list unless the role names a repository-owned server.
bundle_dir/brief.md rendered from the ticket record or the design anchor, plus the attached verdict on a retry.
bundle_dir/output.schema.json, the structured output the seat must return (the role's output shape from N-16, N-17 or N-19).
The role's model id from roles/<role>.json model.claude; never a seat's choice (memory right-size-agent-models).

max_turns, max_budget_usd, wall_clock_seconds, stall_seconds from scheduler/config/seats.json for the role; limits are launcher fields, never prose (rebuild/investigation/02-MAPPING.md#3-dropped-by-the-field-still-carried-here-kill K10).
Every repository path outside the ticket's declared files, expressed as the allow list of the declared files plus a deny of the rest; for a reviewer every write is denied.
Copied from the dispatch; stamped so every downstream gate reads it from the record, not from a file.
sha256 of settings.json, mcp.json, brief.md, output.schema.json, and bundle_hash over the four in that order.
A UUID minted here so N-15 can resume a dead run by id (S04 section 8 item 8). On a rework attempt it is the prior run's session id when N-16 says so.
section.text: Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.bundle.

section.title: Mechanism: the render in the Go service
section.text: Package scheduler/internal/seatlayer in the small Go cut (D09). One function Render(ctx, dispatch) (seat.bundle, error), pure over its inputs: the dispatch record, the role file, the ticket record (or the design anchor text), the seats config and the build-mode state frozen in the dispatch. The same inputs always give the same bytes and the same bundle_hash, which is the proof the checklist asks for.
section.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant S as Store N-01 participant R as seatlayer.Render participant F as roles/ and scheduler/config in the repo at origin/main participant D as $COQ_STATE/seats/bundles/run_id S-->>R: dispatch record (level-triggered list, no seat.bundle yet for run_id) R->>F: read roles/role.json, validate against roles/schema/role.schema.json R->>F: read scheduler/config/seats.json limits for the role R->>S: read ticket record (files, acceptance, title) or the design anchor text R->>R: render settings.json, mcp.json, brief.md, output.schema.json R->>D: write to bundles/.tmp-run_id-pid, fsync, rename to bundles/run_id R->>S: put seat.bundle (idempotency_key = dispatch.id, expected version 0) S-->>R: record.committed or 409 (already rendered by another pass: no-op)
section.step: Read roles/<role>.json from the repository at the sha the dispatch names (origin/main at dispatch time), validate it against roles/schema/role.schema.json. The role schema gains four optional keys by the ticket that builds this node: max_turns, max_budget_usd, wall_clock_seconds, stall_seconds; scheduler/config/seats.json carries the defaults and wins over the role file only when the role file omits a key.

Render settings.json: permissions.allow from the role's allow.tools and allow.commands; permissions.deny from deny.tools, deny.commands, and Edit and Write rules for every path outside the ticket's declared files (claims semantics of factory/bin/claims.sh: a pattern is a bash glob where * crosses /, a bare directory means the subtree). permissions.defaultMode is dontAsk for every host seat, so an allow rule restricts and a miss is a denial, not a prompt (rebuild/investigation/S04-agent-frameworks-seat-contracts.md#8-what-to-carry-forward item 1). hooks is the role's hooks.line set, or hooks.build when build_mode is on; both are empty in slice one. No user layer is referenced.

Render mcp.json with mcpServers {} unless the role names a repository-owned server; the launcher passes --strict-mcp-config so user-scope servers (kubernetes, jenkins, notion, github in ~/.claude.json, L11 F9) never attach.

Render brief.md from the phase template under scheduler/templates/brief-<phase>.md: the ticket id and full title, the declared files, the acceptance commands with their observed exit on main (from N-18), the DAG input and output the ticket declares, the output schema the seat must return, and, on a retry, the verdict record attached verbatim (observations, repro). A brief never contains a rule the launcher enforces by flag; limits appear once as information with the sentence "the launcher enforces these".

Render output.schema.json: the structured output of the phase (N-16 worker.result, N-17 ticket-set.draft, N-19 review.result), copied from that node's record.schema.json so the seat's --json-schema is the same contract the launcher validates.

Write the four files to bundles/.tmp-<run_id>-<pid>/, fsync each, rename the directory to bundles/<run_id>/. A rename is atomic on one filesystem; a second renderer finds the final directory present and skips to step 7.

Put seat.bundle with idempotency_key = dispatch.id and expected version 0. A 409 means another pass committed first; read it, compare bundle_hash, and if the hashes differ write a 500 defect record (two renders of one dispatch disagree) instead of overwriting.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: The Go service (N-06 unit) runs a seat controller goroutine that is level-triggered on every scheduler tick (N-07): it lists dispatch records that have no seat.bundle and no seat.result for the same run_id, and renders each. A dispatch is the only trigger. No pane, no prompt, no herdr call, no human: D08 makes herdr the owner's window only, and the seat.sh bring-up DAG of specs/SPEC-04-herdr-seat-lifecycle.xml#s-seat is a source, not a mechanism (section rejected).
Because the list is recomputed each tick, a lost or duplicate event cannot strand a dispatch (rebuild/investigation/02-MAPPING.md#4-in-the-field-untouched-here-steal T03).

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.what: read role file and config from the repository mirror
wait.fallback: seat.bundle.failed 500 with reason role_unreadable; N-11 counts the attempt

wait.what: read ticket record from the store (gRPC)
wait.fallback: seat.bundle.failed 500 with reason store_unreachable; the tick retries on the next pass, N-11 after 3

wait.what: write and rename the bundle directory
wait.fallback: seat.bundle.failed 500 with reason bundle_io; the temp directory is removed

the bundle directory stays with a bundle.pending marker; the next tick finds the directory, recomputes the hash and puts again (idempotent by dispatch.id); N-06 health reports a dispatch without a committed seat.bundle older than 75 s as a store outage, and N-28 posts one card when the marker survives 3 ticks

section.text: Total bound per dispatch: 75 s. No wait in this node depends on a person or an agent. The build-mode expiry is never waited on: it is read as frozen in the dispatch; N-44 clears the flag at expiry by itself.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: Each step retries 3 times with backoff 1 s, 2 s, 4 s. After the third failure the node writes seat.bundle.failed (code 500, run_id, step, reason, stderr tail) and stops touching that dispatch. N-11 reads it as a failure record: attempt n+1 gets a fresh dispatch and a fresh render; after attempt 3 it is a dead record and N-28 posts exactly one card. Recovery after a service restart: the tick re-lists dispatches without a bundle; a left-over .tmp directory older than 60 s is removed by the render itself before it writes.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Readers: any number of seats read this volume by its anchors; nothing here is per seat. Twenty dispatches in one tick are rendered by a worker pool of size seats.json render_workers (default 4); each has its own temp directory and its own idempotency key, so no two renders share a file.

Collision 1, two passes render the same dispatch (a restart mid-pass, or a second service instance against the rule): the directory rename is atomic, the seat.bundle put is compare-and-swap on version 0 with idempotency_key dispatch.id, so exactly one commits; the loser compares hashes and reports a 500 defect only if the bytes differ.

Collision 2, the role file changes on main while renders are in flight: the render reads the role file at the sha frozen in the dispatch (the mirror's origin/main at dispatch time), so every run of one dispatch sees one role file; a new sha reaches only new dispatches.

Collision 3, two tickets declare overlapping files: not this node's problem to refuse; N-18 refuses at cut and N-14 refuses at start with a store-level unique claim. This node renders the deny list from the ticket as declared.

Collision 4, the build-mode flag flips during a render: the flag is frozen in the dispatch; a run launched under build mode on stays on until it ends, and that is recorded in the bundle so the gate it reaches reads the same value.
Nothing in this node holds a lock a person can forget to release; the only lease is the ticket lease N-02 issued, whose token the bundle carries and never renews.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: Rendered; the launcher may start. Acts: N-15 when the workspace record also exists.

The role file failed its schema, or the ticket declares no files, or the phase has no template. Acts: N-11 as a failure record, and a defect card after 3 because the fault is in the repository, not the run.
An io or store step failed 3 times. Acts: N-11.
section.text: Every code is a row in the shared status code map (section shared-needs); a code not in the map is refused by the store.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.writes: settings.json, mcp.json, brief.md, output.schema.json, bundle.pending (only until the seat.bundle put commits)
path.retention: 7 days after the run's seat.result, or 1 day when no run ever started

section.path: Dry run by default, --apply deletes; registered in N-45 (scheduler/config/cleanup.json entry seat-bundles); never deletes a bundle whose run has no seat.result and whose dispatch is younger than its deadline.

path.cleanup: the render itself (older than 60 s) and cleanup-seat-bundles.sh

section.text: $COQ_STATE resolves through bin/state-root.sh (default ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin), the one resolver (rebuild/investigation/L01-line-scripts.md#8-what-to-carry-forward item 11). Nothing is written into the repository (C35).

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The Go service: read the repository mirror, read and write $COQ_STATE/seats/bundles, gRPC to the store. No GitHub token, no cluster access, no herdr socket.
What the rendered settings give a seat, by role, in slice one:

role.name: worker
role.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash
role.bash: make *, git status|diff|log|add|commit|rev-parse|branch --show-current, the acceptance commands of the ticket
role.deny: Agent, Task, git push, gh *, podman *, herdr *, treehouse *

section.role: The push and the pull request are done by code after the run (N-16); the git read verbs are allowed because their denial made seats conclude they had no shell (L11 F9).

role.name: spec-author
role.write: none in the repository; the output is data returned as structured output
role.deny: Write, Edit, Agent, Task, git push, gh *

role.name: reviewer
role.deny: Write, Edit, Agent, Task, make *, podman *, gh pr review|merge, git push

section.role: A reviewer runs nothing (roles/reviewer.json breadcrumb WO-20261013-b6f3).
section.text: Subagents (Agent, Task) stay denied in slice one for every role: the Agent SDK has no per-subagent wall-clock deadline, so a cap would be prose (S04 section 9 item 4). Lifting it per role is its own ticket with a measured cost.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/seatlayer -run TestRenderDeterministic: two renders of one fixture dispatch give equal bundle_hash

probe run: a user-level hook that writes a marker file is installed on the test host; a seat launched from a bundle with --setting-sources local never writes the marker; the test asserts the file is absent
probe run: ~/.claude.json lists a user MCP server; the seat's claude -p --output-format json reports no MCP server; the test asserts mcp_servers is empty
go test TestDenyPathsFromClaims: ticket files herdr/bin/* yields deny rules for every top-level path except herdr/bin/, and an Edit outside is refused in a probe run (permission_denials names it)

section.item: Deny list comes from the declared files.

item.proof: go test TestBuildModeFrozen: a dispatch with build_mode on yields a bundle with build_mode on even when the store flag is off at render time

section.item: Build mode is frozen in the dispatch.

item.proof: go test TestIdempotentRender: two concurrent renders of one dispatch commit exactly one seat.bundle; the store shows one record, version 1

section.item: One bundle per dispatch under concurrency.

item.proof: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-bundles.sh --dry-run lists the fixture bundle and --apply removes it; a bundle with a live dispatch is listed as kept

section.item: Cleanup script exists and respects liveness.

item.proof: roles/schema/role.schema.json validates roles/worker.json with max_turns, max_budget_usd, wall_clock_seconds, stall_seconds present; make lint passes

section.item: Limits are fields in the role schema.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters in the StatusResponse of scheduler/api/scheduler/v1/scheduler.proto (extended by its own ticket): bundles_rendered, bundles_refused, bundles_failed, render_seconds histogram. The health line shows bundles pending (dispatch without a bundle older than 75 s) as a warning, and the Alerts screen (N-41) shows a seat.bundle.refused as an alert because its fault is in the repository. The Stats screen (N-40) binds to the counters.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: Inspect a bundle: cat $COQ_STATE/seats/bundles/<run_id>/brief.md; sha256sum the four files and compare with the seat.bundle record's hashes.

A refused bundle (412): the fix is in the repository (role file or template); cut a ticket; N-11 already counted the attempt. Never hand-edit a bundle: the launcher checks bundle_hash before it starts and refuses a mismatch with 412.
Cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-bundles.sh [--apply] [--older-than 7d]; registered in N-45 and run by its timer.
Break glass: none in this node. A bundle is never rendered by hand; the owner's one-time break glass (N-42) can force a dispatch, which then renders by this node.
